_comment: Every named part, the claim the specification makes about it, and where that claim was verified. 'checked' is the date the source was actually read, not the date the part was chosen. tools-verify.py fails on any entry without a source or a check date.

removed.reason: TI marks the product LAST TIME BUY, and the DIT4192IDB suffix named in earlier revisions does not exist (only IPW/IPWR, TSSOP-28). The optical S/PDIF output was removed with it.
Cirrus marks it end-of-life; violated the no-NOS rule.

removed.note: removed with the optical S/PDIF output (R4-HDMI1)

removed.reason: DOES NOT EXIST. Invented while resolving R8-PWR1 and entered in this ledger with a family landing page as its source and a 'checked' date that recorded no actual reading. The nearest real member is 0ZCJ0150FF2C, whose Vmax is 8 V and is therefore unusable on a 12 V input. The input fuse is now an explicitly unselected item (spec 16.2).

_evidence_fields.opn_complete: false = `part` is a base/family number, not an orderable one; a suffix must be CHOSEN before it can be verified
_evidence_fields.suffix_evidence: exact-page = the source is a part-details/OPN page for this exact suffix; datasheet = a datasheet was read, but whether its ordering table names this exact suffix is not recorded; family-page = the source cannot establish an orderable suffix at all
_evidence_fields.electrical_evidence: datasheet = the electrical claims in `claim` were read from a datasheet; family-page = they were not
_evidence_fields.lifecycle_evidence: none for every part - no written production-status confirmation has been obtained for any component. This is deliberately uniform rather than inferred from URL shape.
_evidence_fields._why: One boolean (verified_part_specific) conflated exact-suffix identity, electrical verification and lifecycle, so the 21-part gate in spec 16.2 was mechanically wrong: it listed parts whose source was already an exact TI part-details page. Four orthogonal fields, and tools-verify.py generates the 16.2 queue from them.
